# Abramowitz v. Lake, 25-5314 (D.C. Cir. 2026)
**Court:** U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit

**Docket Number:** 25-5314

**Date Decided:** November 10, 2026
The United States District Court for the District of Columbia granted preliminary injunctions to restore Voice of America programming and, after proceedings, granted partial summary judgment and a permanent injunction barring Abramowitz’s removal without Board approval. The district court found it had federal-question jurisdiction over the claim and that the Agency’s actions violated statutory requirements, specifically 22 U.S.C. § 6205(e), which protects the independence of network heads by requiring Board approval for removal.
The United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit reviewed the district court’s order. The appellate court held that the district court had jurisdiction, as Congress did not intend for claims under section 6205(e) to be channeled through the Civil Service Reform Act’s administrative framework. The court concluded that section 6205(e) is constitutionally valid under Article II, as Congress may vest removal authority in department heads, and the Broadcasting Board qualifies as such.
The Agency’s unilateral removal of Abramowitz was contrary to law. The appellate court affirmed the district court’s permanent injunction, holding that injunctive relief was appropriate and necessary to protect the statutory safeguard of the broadcaster’s independence.

# Trump Official Can’t Fire Voice of America Head, Court Says (1)
A three-judge panel for the US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit found Tuesday that US Agency for Global Media leader Kari Lake wasn’t authorized to fire journalist Michael Abramowitz without approval from an independent board.
The US Supreme Court ruled in June to allow Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook to remain in her job while she fights the administration’s effort to fire her. However, the high court ruled the same day in a separate case to expand the president’s power to fire other government officials.

The case is Michael Abramowitz v. Kari Lake, D.C. Cir., No. 25-05314, 11/10/26.

keenable.snippet:
# Appeals court says VOA director was fired illegally by former head Kari Lake
Michael Abramowitz was dismissed by former agency head Kari Lake in August 2025 after refusing an ultimatum: move to a lower-level post or be fired.
Michael Abramowitz, the director of Voice of America, was illegally fired from his role by former agency head Kari Lake, an appeals court panel ruled Tuesday.
Abramowitz was dismissed by Lake in August 2025 after refusing an ultimatum: move to a lower-level post in North Carolina or be fired. Abramowitz refused and was terminated, calling Lake’s move “illegal.”

U.S. District Judge Royce Lamberth, an appointee of President Ronald Reagan who feuded with Lake and at one point threatened to hold her in contempt of court, agreed with Abramowitz that the firing was illegal. Only a Senate-confirmed body called the International Broadcasting Advisory Board, which President Donald Trump dismantled upon taking office for his second term, had the power to fire the VOA director, Lamberth ruled.

On Tuesday, more than a year after that ruling, a three-judge panel on the U.S. Circuit Court for the District of Columbia handed Abramowitz a legal victory by affirming Lamberth’s ruling.
U.S. Circuit Judges Sri Srinivasan and Cornelia Pillard, appointees of President Barack Obama, and Florence Y. Pan, an appointee of President Joe Biden, ruled unanimously.
In a published opinion, Pillard wrote that the protections here are “not a standard employment law, but a durable barrier against any breach of the firewall protecting the journalistic integrity of Voice of America and the affiliate networks.”

This is the Voice of America building in Washington D.C., on May 5, 2025. (AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar, File)

Michael Abramowitz, the director of Voice of America, was illegally fired from his role by former agency head Kari Lake, an appeals court panel ruled Tuesday.

Abramowitz was dismissed by Lake in August 2025 after refusing an ultimatum: move to a lower-level post in North Carolina or be fired. Abramowitz refused and was terminated, calling Lake’s move “illegal.”

The Trump administration doesn’t have the power to remove the Voice of America director as part of its dismantling of the international broadcast network, a federal appeals court ruled.
The case is Michael Abramowitz v. Kari Lake, D.C.
The DC Circuit previously temporarily barred the administration from firing Abramowitz, who has remained on administrative leave, while litigation continued. The case is one of multiple lawsuits filed over the dismantling of Voice of America and USAGM, following Trump’s March 2025 executive order calling for a shutdown of USAGM and other agencies. Lamberth ruled in March of this year that Lake illegally served led USAGM while overseeing the agency’s dissolution.
Kari Lake speaks before a US House committee on June 25, 2025, in Washington.
